words.en: A virgin is someone who has never had sexual intercourse. It can also describe something that is in its original pure or natural condition and has not been touched or changed by people.

words.ex: The barren land cannot grow any crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片贫瘠的土地无法种植任何庄稼。
words.en: If you describe something as barren, you mean that it is not able to produce anything, especially plants or crops.

words.tr:
v. 牵引；拖
n. 牵引；拖
words.ex: He tows his broken car to the garage.
words.ex_cn: 他把坏掉的车拖到修理厂。
words.en: To pull a vehicle or boat along behind another vehicle, using a rope or chain.

words.ex: The wind scatter the leaves everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 风把树叶吹得四处分散。
words.en: To scatter means to throw or drop things over a wide area in an irregular way, or to cause a group of people or animals to move apart in different directions.

words.ex: He uses fertilizer to help his plants grow.
words.ex_cn: 他用肥料帮助植物生长。
words.en: A substance that is added to soil to improve the growth of plants.

words.ex: Farmers use pesticide to kill insects on crops.
words.ex_cn: 农民使用杀虫剂来杀死作物上的昆虫。
words.en: A pesticide is a chemical substance used to kill pests, especially insects, that damage crops or are harmful to human health.

words.tr: adj. 富有成效的；多产的；生产的；
words.ex: He had a productive day and finished all his work.
words.ex_cn: 他度过了富有成效的一天，完成了所有工作。
words.en: Producing or able to produce large amounts of goods, crops, or other commodities.

words.ex: The workers dug a trench to lay the pipe.
words.ex_cn: 工人们挖了一条沟来铺设管道。
words.en: A trench is a long, narrow ditch. In warfare, trenches are dug by troops to provide shelter from enemy fire.

words.ex: Farmers use irrigation to water their crops.
words.ex_cn: 农民使用灌溉来浇灌庄稼。
words.en: Irrigation is the process of supplying water to land or crops to help growth, typically by means of channels.

words.ex: She ate a prune for a healthy snack.
words.ex_cn: 她吃了一颗梅干作为健康零食。
words.en: To prune means to cut off some of the branches of a tree or bush to make it grow better. It can also mean to reduce the extent of something by removing superfluous or unwanted parts.

words.tr:
n. 砍痕；伤痕；斜线号；削减
v. 砍；大幅度削减
words.ex: The tree has a deep slash on its trunk.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树的树干上有一道深深的砍痕。
words.en: To cut something with a sharp object in a violent way; to reduce something by a large amount suddenly.

words.ex: He worked hard and reaped the rewards.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作，获得了回报。
words.en: To reap means to cut and gather a crop, or to obtain something, especially as a result of effort.

words.tr:
v. 生产；获利；
n. 产量；
words.ex: This farm yields a lot of wheat each year.
words.ex_cn: 这个农场每年生产大量小麦。
words.en: If you yield to someone or something, you stop resisting them. If a tree or plant yields fruit or flowers, it produces them.

words.tr:
n. 规模；等级；比例（尺）；刻度；秤；
v. 改变…大小；
words.ex: The scale of the project surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的规模让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A scale is a set of levels or numbers which are used in a particular system of measuring things or are used when comparing things.

words.ex: The boxes are stored in the warehouse.
words.ex_cn: 这些箱子存放在仓库里。
words.en: A warehouse is a large building where raw materials or manufactured goods may be stored before their export or distribution for sale.

words.tr:
n. 贮藏物；隐藏物
v. 贮藏；囤积
words.ex: The treasure hunter found a hoard of gold coins.
words.ex_cn: 寻宝者发现了一堆金币。
words.en: If you hoard things such as food or money, you save or store them, often in secret, because they are valuable or important to you.

words.ex: The forest has abundant water and trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林水源和树木都很丰富。
words.en: If something is abundant, there is a lot of it or it is very common.

words.ex: He eats cereal with milk every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃谷类食品配牛奶。
words.en: A cereal is a grass that is cultivated for the edible components of its grain, composed of the endosperm, germ, and bran.

words.tr:
n. 一摞；一叠；一堆；大烟囱；
v. 把…放成整齐的一摞；
words.ex: He put the books in a stack on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他把书堆成一摞放在桌子上。
words.en: A stack is a pile of things, usually arranged one on top of another.

chapters.name: 经济发展：工农业 - 工业

words.ex: The city has many industrial factories.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市有许多工业工厂。
words.en: Industrial means relating to or characterized by industry.

words.tr:
n. 制造；
v. （用机器大量）制造；虚构；捏造；
words.ex: The manufacture of cars needs many workers.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的制造需要很多工人。
words.en: To manufacture something means to make it in a factory, usually in large quantities.

words.tr: n. 机械（总称）；机械装置；
words.ex: The factory uses old machinery to produce goods.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂使用旧机械来生产产品。
words.en: Machinery refers to machines in general or the parts of a machine that make it work.

words.ex: The mechanical toy moves with batteries.
words.ex_cn: 这个机械玩具用电池驱动。
words.en: Relating to machines or machinery; operated by or involving a machine or machines.

words.ex: The factory will mechanize its production line next year.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂明年将使生产线实现机械化。
words.en: To mechanize something means to change it so that it is done by machines or mechanical processes rather than by human labor.

words.ex: The factory improved its productivity by using new machines.
words.ex_cn: 工厂通过使用新机器提高了生产率。
words.en: Productivity is the rate at which goods are produced or work is completed.

words.ex: He uses an efficient way to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种高效的方法解决数学问题。
words.en: If something or someone is efficient, they are able to do tasks successfully, without wasting time or energy.

words.tr:
n. 工序；过程；
v. 处理；加工；
words.ex: The factory improved the production process.
words.ex_cn: 工厂改进了生产工序。
words.en: A process is a series of actions which are carried out in order to achieve a particular result.

words.tr:
n. 格式；
v. 格式化；
words.ex: The file is in PDF format.
words.ex_cn: 这个文件是PDF格式。
words.en: The way in which something is arranged or set out.

words.ex: He tried to manipulate the results to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他试图操纵结果来赢得比赛。
words.en: To manipulate something means to handle or control it skillfully, often in a way that is considered unfair or dishonest.

words.ex: The government will implement new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将实施新规定。
words.en: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.

words.ex: He will install the new software on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他将在他的电脑上安装新软件。
words.en: To set up or fix in position for use or service.

words.ex: The school will equip the lab with new computers.
words.ex_cn: 学校将为实验室配备新电脑。
words.en: To provide someone or something with the necessary items for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The kitchen has a new washing appliance.
words.ex_cn: 厨房里有一台新的洗衣机。
words.en: An appliance is a device or machine that is used to perform a particular task, especially in the home.

words.ex: He bought a new device to take photos.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一个新设备来拍照。
words.en: A device is an object or machine that has been invented for a particular purpose.

words.tr:
n. 更新；
v. 更新；升级；
words.ex: The app sent me a new update.
words.ex_cn: 应用程序给我发送了一个新更新。
words.en: To make something more modern or up to date, especially by adding new information or changing its design or style.

words.tr:
v. 提升；提高；改进；
n. 增加；改进；
words.ex: He upgraded his phone to get better performance.
words.ex_cn: 他升级了手机以获得更好的性能。
words.en: To upgrade means to improve the quality or usefulness of something, or to raise it to a higher standard. It can also refer to the process of improving or raising something.

words.ex: The company streamlined its hiring process.
words.ex_cn: 公司简化了招聘流程。
words.en: To make something such as a business, organization, or process work more effectively by making it simpler or more efficient.

words.tr:
n. 辩论；讨论；
v. 辩论；讨论；
words.ex: The students had a debate about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学生们就作业进行了一场辩论。
words.en: If you maintain something, you continue to have it, and do not let it stop or grow weaker.

words.ex: He refines his writing every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天完善自己的写作。
words.en: To refine something means to make it purer or to improve it, especially by removing unwanted substances or by making small changes.

words.ex: The machine purifies water by removing dirt.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器通过去除杂质来净化水。
words.en: To purify something means to make it clean and pure by removing dirty or harmful substances from it.

words.ex: The child imitates her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If you imitate someone, you copy what they do or produce.

words.tr:
v. 提取；
n. 摘录；提取物；
words.ex: They extract oil from plants.
words.ex_cn: 他们从植物中提取油。
words.en: To remove or take out something, especially by effort or force.

words.tr:
v. 酿造；沏；酝酿
n. 酿造的饮料；啤酒
words.ex: He brews coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冲咖啡。
words.en: If you brew tea or coffee, you make it by pouring hot water over tea leaves or ground coffee. If you brew beer, you make it by soaking grain in water and then fermenting it.

words.ex: We must eliminate the waste to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须消除浪费以保护环境。
words.en: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.

words.ex: The noise will diminish after midnight.
words.ex_cn: 午夜后噪音会减少。
words.en: If something diminishes, or if something diminishes it, it becomes reduced in size, importance, or intensity.

words.ex: He had a setback when he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，遇到了挫折。
words.en: A setback is an event that delays your progress or reverses some of the progress that you have made.

words.ex: The premise of his argument is that everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他论点的前提是人人平等。
words.en: A premise is a statement or idea that forms the basis for a reasonable line of argument.

words.tr: n. 结构；布局；配置；外形
words.ex: The configuration of the computer is very simple.
words.ex_cn: 这台电脑的配置非常简单。
words.en: The arrangement of parts or elements in a particular form, figure, or combination.

words.ex: The steam condenses into water when it touches the cold glass.
words.ex_cn: 当蒸汽接触到冷的玻璃时，会凝结成水。
words.en: If you condense something, especially a piece of writing or a speech, you make it shorter, usually by including only the most important parts.

words.tr:
n. 合金
v. 把…铸成合金
words.ex: He made a strong alloy from copper and zinc.
words.ex_cn: 他用铜和锌制造了一种坚固的合金。
words.en: An alloy is a metal made by combining two or more metallic elements, especially to give greater strength or resistance to corrosion.

words.ex: The electrician fixed the broken light.
words.ex_cn: 电工修好了坏掉的灯。
words.en: An electrician is a person whose job is to install and repair electrical equipment.

words.ex: The wind generates electricity.
words.ex_cn: 风产生电力。
words.en: To generate something means to cause it to begin and develop.

words.ex: He used a match to ignite the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他用火柴点燃了火。
words.en: If you ignite something or if it ignites, it starts burning or explodes.

words.ex: The beer left foam on the top of the glass.
words.ex_cn: 啤酒在杯子顶部留下了一层泡沫。
words.en: Foam is a mass of small bubbles that are formed in or on a liquid.

words.tr: v. 隔离；使隔热；使隔音；使绝缘
words.ex: The walls insulate the house from cold air.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁将房子与冷空气隔离开。
words.en: To insulate something means to protect it from heat, cold, noise, or electricity by covering it in a material that prevents it from passing through.

words.tr:
n. 箔；陪衬物
v. 阻止；挫败
words.ex: He used foil to wrap the sandwich.
words.ex_cn: 他用锡纸包住了三明治。
words.en: To prevent someone from succeeding in their plans or intentions, especially by doing something clever or unexpected.

words.tr:
n. 小块；碎片；废金属；吵架
v. 废弃；取消
adj. 废弃的
words.ex: He picked up a scrap of paper from the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他从地上捡起一张纸片。
words.en: A scrap is a small piece or amount of something, especially one that is left over after the greater part has been used. It can also mean to discard or get rid of something as being no longer useful or necessary.

words.tr:
n. 筛子；滤器
v. 筛；滤
words.ex: He used a sieve to separate sand from pebbles.
words.ex_cn: 他用筛子把沙子和石子分开。
words.en: A sieve is a tool consisting of a wire or plastic mesh held in a frame, used for separating solids from liquids or larger particles from smaller ones.

words.ex: The nail fits into the groove.
words.ex_cn: 钉子卡在槽里。
words.en: A groove is a long, narrow space or cut in a surface, often made to guide the movement of something or to hold something in place. It can also refer to a settled routine or way of doing things that is hard to change.

words.ex: The door opens on a metal hinge.
words.ex_cn: 这扇门装在一个金属枢纽上。
words.en: A hinge is a piece of metal, wood, or plastic that is used to join two things together so that one of them can swing or move freely.

words.ex: He shifted the gear to slow down the car.
words.ex_cn: 他换挡以减慢车速。
words.en: Gear refers to a toothed wheel that works with others to alter the relation between the speed of a driving mechanism (such as the engine of a vehicle) and the speed of the driven parts (the wheels). It can also mean equipment that is used for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The clever boy solved the math problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个聪明的男孩很快解决了这道数学题。
words.en: Someone who is clever is intelligent and able to understand things easily or plan things well.

words.ex: The workers used a hoist to lift the heavy beams.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用吊升机械吊起沉重的梁。
words.en: To hoist something means to lift or pull it up to a higher position, usually using some kind of equipment such as a crane or pulley.

words.tr:
n. 螺丝钉；
v. 拧紧；
words.ex: He tightened the screw with a screwdriver.
words.ex_cn: 他用螺丝刀拧紧了螺丝钉。
words.en: A screw is a metal object similar to a nail, with a raised spiral line around it. Screws are used to fasten things together.

words.ex: He used a clamp to hold the wood together.
words.ex_cn: 他用夹具把木头固定在一起。
words.en: A clamp is a device that holds two things firmly together. As a verb, to clamp means to hold or fasten something tightly.

words.ex: Oil helps to lubricate the engine parts.
words.ex_cn: 油有助于润滑发动机部件。
words.en: To apply a substance such as oil or grease to (something) in order to minimize friction and allow smooth movement.

words.ex: The needle will pierce the skin.
words.ex_cn: 针会刺穿皮肤。
words.en: If a sharp object pierces something, or if you pierce something with a sharp object, the object goes into it and makes a hole in it.

words.ex: The internal parts of the machine need repair.
words.ex_cn: 机器的内部零件需要修理。
words.en: Internal is used to describe things that exist or happen inside a particular person, object, or place.

words.ex: A car has many components, like wheels and engines.
words.ex_cn: 汽车有许多部分，比如轮子和发动机。
words.en: A component is a part of a larger whole, especially a part that can be separated from or attached to a system.

words.ex: The table is made of a composite material.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是由一种合成材料制成的。
words.en: A composite is something that is made up of several different parts or materials.

words.tr:
n. 成分；
adj. 构成的；
words.ex: Sugar is a constituent of soda.
words.ex_cn: 糖是苏打水的一种成分。
words.en: A constituent is a part of a whole. In politics, a constituent is a person who is represented by an elected official.

words.tr:
n. 包；包裹；
v. 包装；
words.ex: He bought a package of cookies.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一包饼干。
words.en: A package is a wrapped container or a set of objects wrapped in paper or packed in a box.

chapters.name: 经济发展：商业 - 经济

words.ex: The country's economy is growing fast.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家的经济正在快速增长。
words.en: The economy of a country or region is the system by which money, industry, and trade are organized.

words.ex: Wheat is a basic commodity in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 小麦在许多国家是一种基本商品。
words.en: A commodity is something that is bought and sold.

words.tr:
n. 金融；财务；
v. 提供资金；
words.ex: He works in finance in New York.
words.ex_cn: 他在纽约从事金融工作。
words.en: Finance is the management of large amounts of money, especially by governments or large companies.

words.ex: The monetary policy affects prices.
words.ex_cn: 货币政策影响价格。
words.en: Monetary means relating to money, especially the total amount of money in a country.

words.ex: Under these circumstances, we had to cancel the trip.
words.ex_cn: 在这种情况下，我们不得不取消旅行。
words.en: A circumstance is a fact or event that makes a situation the way it is.

words.ex: The government made a fiscal decision to lower taxes.
words.ex_cn: 政府做出了降低税收的财政决定。
words.en: Fiscal is used to describe something that relates to government money or public money, especially taxes.

words.ex: He invests money in stocks.
words.ex_cn: 他投资股票。
words.en: If you invest in something, or if you invest a sum of money, you use your money in a way that you hope will increase its value, for example by putting it in a bank, or buying shares or property.

words.ex: The company is a legal entity.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是一个法律实体。
words.en: An entity is something that exists separately from other things and has a clear identity of its own.

words.tr: n. 企业家；创业者；承包人；
words.ex: He is an entrepreneur who started a small coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位创办了小型咖啡店的企业家。
words.en: An entrepreneur is a person who organizes and operates a business or businesses, taking on greater than normal financial risks in order to do so.

words.tr:
v. 有益于；有助于；
n. 利益；好处；
words.ex: Exercise benefits your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼有益于你的健康。
words.en: A benefit is something that helps you or improves your life in some way.

words.ex: The new job enriched his life.
words.ex_cn: 这份新工作使他的生活富裕起来。
words.en: To enrich something means to improve its quality, often by adding something to it.

words.ex: The gross income of the company is $5 million.
words.ex_cn: 公司的总收入是500万美元。
words.en: If you describe something as gross, you mean it is very obvious, unacceptable, or unpleasant.

words.tr:
n. 总计；集合体
adj. 合计的；总的
v. （使）聚集；聚合；总计为
words.ex: The aggregate of all sales this month is $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 本月所有销售额的总计是5万美元。
words.en: An aggregate is a number of things or people that are considered as a group or a whole.

words.tr: adj. 家庭的；国内的；驯养的；
words.ex: She prefers domestic chores over going out.
words.ex_cn: 她更喜欢做家务而不是外出。
words.en: Domestic means relating to the home, family, or household affairs. It can also refer to something that is made or produced within a country and not imported.

words.tr: adj. 自治的；有自治权的；自主的；
words.ex: The region has autonomous control over its education system.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区对其教育系统拥有自治权。
words.en: An autonomous organization, country, or region is independent and has the freedom to govern itself.

words.tr: n. 自主权；自治权；自治；
words.ex: The region demands autonomy from the central government.
words.ex_cn: 该地区要求从中央政府获得自主权。
words.en: Autonomy is the ability or condition of being self-governing; independence in one's thoughts or actions.

words.ex: The company will consolidate two departments next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将合并两个部门。
words.en: To consolidate something means to make it stronger, more secure, or more solid.

words.ex: The doctor tried to stabilize the patient's heart rate.
words.ex_cn: 医生试图稳定病人的脉搏。
words.en: To stabilize something means to make it stable or to prevent it from changing or declining.

words.ex: The stability of the table prevents it from wobbling.
words.ex_cn: 桌子的固定防止它摇晃。
words.en: The state of being stable; the quality of being unchanging.

words.ex: The instability of the bridge made people afraid to cross it.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥的不稳定让人们不敢过桥。
words.en: Instability is the state of being unstable, especially in a political or economic context, where it refers to a lack of stability or the tendency to change or fail suddenly.

words.tr: v. 使浸透；使湿透；使满；使饱和
words.ex: The sponge will saturate if you pour too much water.
words.ex_cn: 如果你倒太多水，海绵会吸满。
words.en: To saturate something means to make it completely wet, or to fill it completely with something so that no more can be added.

words.ex: There is a tendency for people to use phones before bed.
words.ex_cn: 人们在睡觉前使用手机是一种趋势。
words.en: A tendency is a likelihood of behaving in a particular way or going in a particular direction, which is often bad or undesirable.

words.ex: The scope of this project includes three cities.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的范围包括三个城市。
words.en: The range of one's perceptions, thoughts, or actions.

words.ex: Many people lost jobs during the recession.
words.ex_cn: 在经济不景气期间，许多人失去了工作。
words.en: A recession is a period when the economy of a country is not doing well, industrial production and business activity are at a low level, and many people are unemployed.

words.ex: The country is facing an economic crisis.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正面临经济危机。
words.en: A crisis is a situation in which something or someone is affected by one or more very serious problems.

words.ex: The price of oil fluctuates every day.
words.ex_cn: 油价每天都在波动。
words.en: To fluctuate means to change or vary frequently and unpredictably.

words.tr: v. 膨胀；使充气；夸口；吹嘘
words.ex: He tries to inflate the balloon with his mouth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用嘴把气球吹大。
words.en: To inflate something means to cause it to increase in size by filling it with air or gas. It can also refer to increasing the amount of money in circulation, leading to a decrease in its value.

words.ex: The noise from the construction caused a disturbance.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工地的噪音造成了干扰。
words.en: A disturbance is an event or situation in which people behave in a noisy or violent way, or something that interrupts what you are doing.

words.tr:
n. 刻板印象；陈规老套
v. 对…存有成见；把…模式化
words.ex: He broke the stereotype that boys cannot cry.
words.ex_cn: 他打破了男孩不能哭的刻板印象。
words.en: A stereotype is a fixed general image or set of characteristics that a lot of people believe represent a particular type of person or thing.

words.tr:
n. 猛跌；衰退；萧条期
v. 急剧下降；暴跌；重重地坐下（或倒下）
words.ex: The company's sales went into a slump last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月，这家公司的销售额下滑了。
words.en: If something such as the value of something slumps, it falls suddenly and by a large amount.

words.tr:
n. 幻灯片；滑梯；
v. （使）滑动；下滑；
words.ex: He showed a slide of his vacation photos.
words.ex_cn: 他展示了一张他度假照片的幻灯片。
words.en: To move smoothly along a surface while maintaining continuous contact with it; to pass or move quietly or smoothly; a structure with a smooth sloping surface for children to slide down; a decline from a higher to a lower level or status.

words.tr:
v. 跌倒；摔倒；暴跌
n. 摔倒；混乱；暴跌
words.ex: The child tumble down the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 孩子从楼梯上跌倒了。
words.en: If someone or something tumbles, they fall quickly and suddenly, often turning over or spinning as they fall.

words.tr:
v. 投入；跳入
n. 跳进；骤降
words.ex: He plunged into the cold water.
words.ex_cn: 他跳进了冰冷的水里。
words.en: If something or someone plunges in a particular direction, especially into water, they fall, rush, or throw themselves in that direction.

words.ex: The rope is slack and hangs loosely.
words.ex_cn: 绳子是松弛的，垂挂着。
words.en: If something is slack, it is loose and not firmly stretched or tightly in position. It can also describe a period of low activity or a lack of effort in work or activity.

words.tr:
n. 下降；衰退；
v. 下降；衰退；
words.ex: There was a sharp decline in sales last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月销售额大幅下降。
words.en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

words.tr: v. 压下；降低；使沮丧；使不活泼；使萧条
words.ex: He depresses the button to start the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他按下按钮启动机器。
words.en: If something depresses you, it makes you feel sad and disappointed.

words.ex: He felt deep depression after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到深深的抑郁。
words.en: A period during which business, employment, and stock-market values decline severely or remain at a very low level of activity.

words.tr:
v. （使）倾斜；（使）偏向
n. 倾斜；企图
words.ex: The boy tilt the cup and spill the water.
words.ex_cn: 男孩把杯子倾斜，水洒了出来。
words.en: If you tilt an object or if it tilts, it moves into a sloping position with one end or side higher than the other.

words.ex: The old wall began to crumble after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 旧墙在雨后开始坍塌。
words.en: If something crumbles, or if you crumble it, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.

words.ex: The medicine helped revive the sick man.
words.ex_cn: 这剂药帮助这位病人恢复了生机。
words.en: To revive something means to bring it back to life, consciousness, or use, or to make it active or successful again.

words.ex: He needs time for recovery after the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他手术后需要时间恢复。
words.en: The process of becoming well again after an illness or injury, or the process of returning to a normal condition after a period of difficulty.

words.ex: The bright light was a stimulus for the baby to open his eyes.
words.ex_cn: 明亮的光线是让婴儿睁开眼睛的刺激物。
words.en: Something that causes growth or activity.

words.tr: v. 扩大；膨胀；更充分地阐述；
words.ex: The company plans to expand its business to other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司计划将其业务扩大到其他国家。
words.en: To increase in size, number, or importance, or to make something increase in this way.

words.tr: v. 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；
words.ex: Plants thrive in sunny places.
words.ex_cn: 植物在阳光充足的地方茁壮成长。
words.en: To thrive means to grow or develop well or vigorously.

words.ex: He worked hard and prospered in business.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作，在商业上取得了成功。
words.en: If people or businesses prosper, they are successful and do well.

words.ex: The city had an economic boom after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 新工厂开业后，这座城市迎来了经济繁荣。
words.en: If there is a boom in the economy, there is an increase in economic activity, for example in the amount of things that are being bought and sold.

words.ex: The price of oil soared last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月石油价格骤升。
words.en: To rise or increase dramatically in amount or level.

words.tr:
n. 螺旋形；陡升或骤降；
v. 螺旋式上升（或下降）；
adj. 螺旋形的；
words.ex: The snail moved along a spiral path.
words.ex_cn: 蜗牛沿着一个螺旋形的路径爬行。
words.en: A spiral is a shape which winds round and round, with each curve above or outside the previous one.

words.tr: adj. 陡峭的；急剧升降的；
words.ex: The mountain has a steep path.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一条陡峭的小路。
words.en: A steep slope or hill is one that is at a sharp angle, rather than being flat or gradual.

words.tr:
v. 作嗡嗡声；飞驰；陡升
n. 直线上升；激增；嗡嗡声
words.ex: The bee zooms around the flowers.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂在花丛中嗡嗡飞舞。
words.en: to move quickly or suddenly with a loud, low, continuous noise, or to make something do this

words.ex: He will rectify the mistake tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会纠正这个错误。
words.en: If you rectify something that is wrong, you change it so that it becomes correct or satisfactory.

words.ex: The factory has a quota of 1000 units per day.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂每天有1000件的配额。
words.en: A quota is the limited number or quantity of something which is officially allowed.

words.ex: The company's revenue increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的收入去年增加了。
words.en: Revenue is the income that a company, organization, or government receives regularly.

words.ex: The government imposed a new tax on sugar.
words.ex_cn: 政府对糖征收了一项新税。
words.en: To impose means to officially force a rule, tax, punishment, etc. to be obeyed or received.

words.tr:
n. 问题；重要议题；发行（物）；
v. 发行；
words.ex: The main issue is lack of money.
words.ex_cn: 主要问题是缺乏资金。
words.en: An issue is an important subject or problem that people are talking about or arguing about.

words.ex: He kept the receipt for his new shoes.
words.ex_cn: 他保留了新鞋的收据。
words.en: A receipt is a piece of paper that you get from someone as proof that they have received money or goods from you.

words.tr:
n. 库存；股票；家畜；
v. 备有；贮存；
words.ex: The store has low stock of winter coats.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店的冬衣库存很少。
words.en: The supply of goods available for sale in a store; the capital raised by a company through the issue of shares.

words.tr: n. 公牛；大型雄性动物；胡扯；废话
words.ex: The bull charged at the matador.
words.ex_cn: 公牛冲向了斗牛士。
words.en: A bull is a male animal of the cattle family, or a male elephant, whale, or other large animal. In finance, a bull is someone who buys shares in the expectation that their value will rise.

words.tr: n. 被除数；股份红利；股息
words.ex: In 12 ÷ 3 = 4, the dividend is 12.
words.en: A dividend is a sum of money paid regularly (typically annually) by a company to its shareholders out of its profits (or reserves).

words.tr: n. 安全；保障；防护措施；
words.ex: The school improved security to protect students.
words.ex_cn: 学校加强了安全措施以保护学生。
words.en: Security refers to the state of being free from danger or threat, or measures taken to ensure safety.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；重大的；实质性的；
words.ex: He made a substantial profit from the sale.
words.ex_cn: 他从这次销售中获得了大量的利润。
words.en: Something that is substantial is large in size, amount, or importance.

words.ex: The farm has a surplus of apples this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年农场苹果过剩。
words.en: A surplus is an amount of something that is extra or more than what is needed.

words.ex: He tried to curb his horse with the reins.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用缰绳勒住马。
words.en: If you curb something, you control it and keep it within limits.

words.ex: The circulation of blood keeps us alive.
words.ex_cn: 血液的循环让我们活着。
words.en: The movement of something such as money or goods from place to place or from person to person; the number of copies of a newspaper or magazine that are sold.

words.ex: The clearance of trash improved the park's appearance.
words.ex_cn: 清理垃圾改善了公园的外观。
words.en: Clearance refers to the process of removing or getting rid of something, or the space that is needed for one thing to move past another. It can also refer to the permission given for something to happen or be done.

words.ex: The team made a smart strategy to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队制定了一项聪明的策略来赢得比赛。
words.en: A strategy is a plan that you use in order to achieve something.

words.tr: adj. 一年一次的；每年的；
words.ex: The school holds an annual sports day.
words.ex_cn: 学校每年举行一次运动会。
words.en: An annual event happens once every year.

words.tr:
n. 账户；叙述；账目；
v. 占…；说明；
words.ex: I opened a bank account last week.
words.ex_cn: 我上周开了一家银行账户。
words.en: An account is a detailed report or description of an event or situation.

words.tr:
n. 预算；预算金额；
adj. 廉价的；花钱少的；
v. 为 ... 做预算；
words.ex: We made a budget for our vacation.
words.ex_cn: 我们为旅行制定了一个预算。
words.en: A budget is a plan that shows how much money a person or organization will earn and how much they will need or be able to spend.

words.ex: The country has a budget deficit this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年这个国家的预算不足额。
words.en: A deficit is the amount by which something, especially a sum of money, is too small.

words.ex: He felt the repression of his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到了压抑自己真实情感的痛苦。
words.en: Repression is the act of subduing someone or something by force, or the state of being subdued in such a way.

words.ex: The law constrains companies from polluting rivers.
words.ex_cn: 法律约束公司不得污染河流。
words.en: To constrain someone or something means to limit their development or force them to behave in a particular way.

words.ex: The car will accelerate when you press the gas.
words.ex_cn: 当你踩油门时，汽车会加速。
words.en: To accelerate means to start to go faster or to make something start to go faster.

chapters.name: 经济发展：商业 - 贸易

words.tr:
n. 计划；方案；项目；课题；
v. 投射；预计；
words.ex: He presented his school project to the class.
words.ex_cn: 他向全班展示了他的学校计划。
words.en: A project is a piece of work that is planned or intended, or a large piece of work that is done by a group of people.

words.tr:
n. 阶段；时期；
v. 分阶段进行；
words.ex: The project is in its final phase.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正处于最后阶段。
words.en: A phase is a particular stage in a process or in the gradual development of something.

words.ex: He lost all his property in the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他在火灾中失去了所有财产。
words.en: Something owned; a possession.

words.tr: n. 有价值的人或物；长处；
words.ex: He is an asset to the team because he works hard.
words.ex_cn: 他是个有价值的人，因为他工作努力。
words.en: An asset is something valuable that an individual, corporation, or country owns or controls with the expectation that it will provide a future benefit.

words.ex: The expense of the trip was higher than expected.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅行的费用比预期的要高。
words.en: An expense is the amount of money that you spend on something.

words.tr: v. 扩大；膨胀；更充分地阐述；
words.ex: The company plans to expand its business to other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司计划将其业务扩大到其他国家。
words.en: To increase in size, number, or importance, or to make something increase in this way.

words.ex: The family reduced their monthly expenditure.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭减少了每月的开支。
words.en: Expenditure is the spending of money on something, or the money that is spent on something.

words.tr:
adj. 在头顶上的；
adv. 在空中；
words.ex: The overhead light is too bright.
words.ex_cn: 头顶上的灯太亮了。
words.en: You use overhead to indicate that something is above you or above the place that you are talking about.

words.tr:
n. 交换；兑换；交易所；
v. 交换；
words.ex: They made an exchange of books.
words.ex_cn: 他们进行了书籍的交换。
words.en: If you exchange something, you give it to someone and receive something else in return.

words.ex: The new law gave impetus to environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 新法律为环境保护提供了推动力。
words.en: Something that gives a process impetus or an impetus makes it happen or progress more quickly.

words.ex: The car exceeded the speed limit.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车超过了限速。
words.en: To be greater in quantity, degree, or intensity than something else.

words.tr:
n. 决策人；行政官；管理人员；
adj. 行政的；决策的；
words.ex: The executive decided to launch the new product.
words.ex_cn: 这位决策人决定推出新产品。
words.en: An executive is a person who has a senior management position in a business or other organization.

words.ex: Good management helps a company grow.
words.ex_cn: 良好的管理有助于公司发展。
words.en: The control and organization of something, especially a business and its employees.

words.tr:
v. 实施；传导（电、热）；
n. 行为；举止；
words.ex: The company will conduct a survey next week.
words.ex_cn: 公司将在下周进行一项调查。
words.en: To organize and carry out a particular activity.

words.tr:
n. 抓痕；刮伤；
v. 抓搔；刮；
words.ex: The cat left a scratch on the door.
words.ex_cn: 猫在门上抓出了一道抓痕。
words.en: If you scratch something, you rub your fingernails or claws against it, often because it is itchy or irritating.

words.ex: They established a new school in the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们在村里建立了一所新学校。
words.en: To set up or create something, such as an organization or a system, on a firm or permanent basis.

words.ex: He accumulates coins from different countries.
words.ex_cn: 他收集来自不同国家的硬币。
words.en: To accumulate means to gradually gather or acquire an increasing number or quantity of something.

words.ex: He speculates that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you speculate about something, you make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.

words.tr:
n. 冒险事业；商业冒险；投机；
v. 冒险；投机；
words.ex: He started a new venture in technology.
words.ex_cn: 他创办了一项新的科技冒险事业。
words.en: If you venture somewhere, you go somewhere that might be dangerous. If you venture a question or statement, you say it in an uncertain way because you are afraid it might be stupid or wrong.

words.ex: The government made a new regulation to control pollution.
words.ex_cn: 政府出台了一项新管理措施来控制污染。
words.en: A regulation is an official rule or order.

words.ex: He accepted a nominal fee for the service.
words.ex_cn: 他为这项服务收取了微不足道的费用。
words.en: If you say that something is nominal, you mean that it is very small in comparison to the real value or importance of something.

words.ex: The big company owns a subsidiary that makes phones.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司拥有一家生产手机的附属公司。
words.en: A subsidiary is a company which is part of a larger and more important company.

words.ex: The local company is an affiliate of the big global brand.
words.ex_cn: 这家本地公司是这个全球大品牌的分公司。
words.en: If an organization is affiliated with another larger organization, it is officially connected with the larger organization or is a member of it.

words.ex: This brand has an exclusive design.
words.ex_cn: 这个品牌拥有独有的设计。
words.en: Something that is exclusive is available only to particular people, and not to everyone.

words.tr:
adj. 合作的；
n. 合作社；
words.ex: The two companies made a cooperative effort to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 两家公司合作努力解决问题。
words.en: A cooperative is an organization or business that is owned and run jointly by its members, who share the profits or benefits.

words.ex: The bank recorded the transaction quickly.
words.ex_cn: 银行迅速记录了这笔交易。
words.en: A transaction is an instance of buying or selling something; a business deal.

words.ex: The corporate office is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的总部在纽约。
words.en: Corporate relates to large companies or to a particular large company.

words.tr:
n. 委员会；佣金；
v. 委托；
words.ex: The commission met to discuss the new law.
words.ex_cn: 委员会开会讨论新法律。
words.en: A commission is a group of people who have been appointed to find out about something or to control something, or the act of doing this. It can also refer to a sum of money that is paid to someone for selling something, which is usually a percentage of the value of the goods sold.

words.tr: n. 专题讨论会；研讨会
words.ex: He spoke at a symposium about climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个关于气候变化的研讨会上发言。
words.en: A symposium is a conference or meeting to discuss a particular subject.

words.tr: n. 营业额；人员流动率；周转率；
words.ex: The store's turnover increased last month.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店上个月的营业额增加了。
words.en: The amount of money taken by a business in a particular period.

words.ex: He got a patent for his new invention.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的新发明获得了专利。
words.en: A patent is an official right to be the only person or company allowed to make or sell a new product for a certain period of time.

words.tr:
adj. 贸易的；商业的；
n. 广告；
words.ex: The commercial ship sailed to another country.
words.ex_cn: 这艘贸易船只驶向了另一个国家。
words.en: Commercial relates to the business of buying and selling goods and services.

words.ex: The company has a famous trademark on its logo.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司在其标志上有一个著名的标记。
words.en: A trademark is a recognizable sign, design, or expression which identifies products or services of a particular source from those of others.

words.ex: The company used a short slogan to attract customers.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司用了一个简短的口号来吸引顾客。
words.en: A short and striking or memorable phrase used in advertising or politics.

words.ex: The evidence warrants a new investigation.
words.ex_cn: 证据使新的调查成为必要。
words.en: If something warrants a particular action, it makes the action seem necessary or appropriate for the circumstances.

words.tr: n. 保证；保修单；保证书
words.ex: The phone comes with a one-year warranty.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一年的保修期。
words.en: A warranty is a written guarantee, often given to the purchaser of an article by its manufacturer, promising to repair or replace it if necessary within a specified period of time.

words.ex: The engineer checked the specification for the machine.
words.ex_cn: 工程师检查了机器的规格。
words.en: A specification is a detailed description of the design and materials used to make something.

words.ex: I am awaiting the bus.
words.ex_cn: 我正在等公交车。
words.en: If you await someone or something, you wait for them.

words.ex: I asked for a refund after the product broke.
words.ex_cn: 产品坏了之后，我要求退款。
words.en: A refund is a sum of money that is returned to you, for example because you have paid too much or because you have returned goods to a shop.

words.tr: v. 弥补；兑换；付清；赎回；履行
words.ex: He worked hard to redeem his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作来弥补自己的错误。
words.en: To redeem something means to get it back by paying a sum of money or by doing something to compensate for a fault or mistake.

words.ex: He will repay the loan next month.
words.ex_cn: 他下个月会偿还贷款。
words.en: If you repay a loan or a debt, you pay back the money that you owe to the person who you borrowed or took it from.

words.ex: He incurred a fine for speeding.
words.ex_cn: 他因超速而招致了一笔罚款。
words.en: If you incur something unpleasant, it happens to you because of something you have done.

words.ex: He received compensation for his injured leg.
words.ex_cn: 他因腿部受伤获得了赔偿。
words.en: Compensation is something, typically money, awarded to someone in recognition of loss, suffering, or injury.

words.ex: He paid the first installment last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周支付了第一期分期付款。
words.en: An installment is one of the amounts, usually equal, into which a debt is divided for payment at stated intervals over a fixed period.

words.ex: The store made an inventory of all the products.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有商品做了一份清单。
words.en: An inventory is a detailed list of all the items in a place.

words.tr:
n. 租契；
v. 出租；
words.ex: He signed a lease for the apartment.
words.ex_cn: 他签了公寓的租契。
words.en: A lease is a legal agreement by which the owner of a building, a piece of land, or something such as a car allows someone else to use it for a period of time in return for money.

words.tr:
adj. 成熟的；
v. 成熟；
words.ex: He is a mature student who works full-time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位成熟的学生，全职工作。
words.en: When something or someone matures, they become fully grown or developed. In finance, a mature investment is one that has reached the end of its term and is ready to be paid out.

words.tr: adj. 赚大钱的；获利多的；
words.ex: He took a lucrative job at a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他去了一家科技公司做一份赚大钱的工作。
words.en: A lucrative activity or job is one that you can earn a lot of money from.

words.ex: The store sells cheap merchandise.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售廉价商品。
words.en: Goods to be bought and sold.

words.tr:
n. 禁止贸易令；禁运
v. 禁止…的贸易；禁运
words.ex: The country placed an embargo on imported goods.
words.ex_cn: 该国对进口商品实施了禁运。
words.en: An embargo is an official order to stop trade with another country.

words.ex: The fence is a barrier to animals.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏是动物的障碍。
words.en: A barrier is something such as a rule, law, or policy that makes it difficult or impossible for something to happen or be achieved.

words.tr:
v. 交换；
n. 交换；
words.ex: They swap books every week.
words.ex_cn: 他们每周交换书籍。
words.en: If you swap something with someone, you give it to them and receive a different thing in exchange.

words.ex: The withdrawal of the offer surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 撤销这项提议让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The act of removing or taking something away, especially money from a bank account, or the process of stopping taking a drug or medicine.

words.ex: The teacher will revoke his privilege to use the computer.
words.ex_cn: 老师将撤销他使用电脑的权限。
words.en: If someone in authority revokes something such as a law, license, or agreement, they cancel it.

words.tr:
v. 豁免；
adj. 被免除的；
words.ex: The school exempted him from the test.
words.ex_cn: 学校免除了他的考试。
words.en: If someone or something is exempt from a particular rule, duty, or obligation, they do not have to follow it or do it.

words.tr: n. 关税；税率；（旅馆、饭店等的）价目表
words.ex: The government raised the tariff on imported cars.
words.ex_cn: 政府提高了进口汽车的关税。
words.en: A tariff is a tax that a government collects on goods coming into a country.

words.tr:
v. 征收；征税；征募
n. 征兵；征税
words.ex: The government will levy a new tax next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将征收一项新税。
words.en: To levy means to impose or collect a tax, fee, or fine. It can also refer to the act of enlisting or drafting individuals into military service.

words.ex: The new plan incorporates feedback from students.
words.ex_cn: 新计划包含了学生的反馈。
words.en: If one thing incorporates another thing, it includes the other thing.

words.ex: The latent talent in the child became clear after years of practice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子潜在的才能在多年练习后显现出来。
words.en: Latent is used to describe something which is hidden and not obvious at the moment, but which may develop further in the future.

words.ex: He has a monopoly on selling ice cream in this town.
words.ex_cn: 他在这座小镇上垄断了冰淇淋的销售。
words.en: If a company, person, or state has a monopoly on something such as an industry, they have complete control over it, so that it is impossible for others to become involved in it.

words.ex: He took out a mortgage to buy his first house.
words.ex_cn: 他申请了一笔抵押贷款来购买他的第一套房子。
words.en: A mortgage is a loan of money which you get from a bank or building society in order to buy a house.

words.ex: He computes the total cost quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快算出总成本。
words.en: If you compute a total, amount, or result, you calculate it.

words.ex: The boss gave a positive appraisal of his work.
words.ex_cn: 老板对他的工作给予了积极的评估。
words.en: An appraisal is a judgement or assessment of the value, nature, or quality of something or someone.

words.ex: The old painting was sold at an auction.
words.ex_cn: 那幅旧画在拍卖会上被卖出了。
words.en: An auction is a public sale where goods or property are sold to the highest bidder.

words.ex: He won the spelling contest.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了拼写比赛。
words.en: A contest is a competition or a struggle for victory between individuals or groups.

words.ex: Two companies compete for the same customers.
words.ex_cn: 两家公司为争夺相同的客户而竞争。
words.en: If you compete with someone for something, you try to get it for yourself and stop the other person getting it. You can also say that two people compete for something that they both want.

words.ex: He faced his adversary in the final match.
words.ex_cn: 他在决赛中对阵对手。
words.en: An adversary is someone who you are competing with, or who is opposing you or what you are trying to do.

words.ex: He made a commitment to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺按时完成这个项目。
words.en: A commitment is something that regularly takes up some of your time because of an agreement you have made or because of responsibilities that you have.

words.ex: They have a reciprocal agreement to help each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们有一个互相帮助的互惠协议。
words.en: A reciprocal action or agreement involves two people or groups who do the same thing to each other or agree to help each other in a similar way.

words.ex: The default setting is on.
words.ex_cn: 默认设置是开启的。
words.en: If a person, company, or country defaults on something that they have legally agreed to do, such as paying a debt or keeping to an agreement, they fail to do it.

words.ex: He will cancel the meeting tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会取消会议。
words.en: If you cancel something that has been arranged, you stop it from happening. If you cancel an order for goods or services, you tell the person or organization supplying them that you no longer wish to receive them.

words.ex: They will negotiate the price with the seller.
words.ex_cn: 他们会与卖家协商价格。
words.en: If people negotiate with each other or negotiate an agreement, they talk about a problem or a situation such as a business arrangement in order to solve the problem or complete the arrangement.

words.tr:
n. 合同；契约；
v. 收缩；
words.ex: They signed a contract to buy the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份购买房子的合同。
words.en: A contract is a legal agreement between two or more parties. It can also mean to become smaller or tighter, or to catch a disease.

words.tr: n. 一件物品或商品；项目；一则；
words.ex: This item is on sale for $5.
words.ex_cn: 这件商品正在促销，售价5美元。
words.en: An item is one of a collection or list of objects.

words.ex: You must abide by the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: If you can't abide someone or something, you dislike them very much.

chapters.name: 人文社会：智慧结晶 - 璀璨艺术

words.ex: The painting has a simple aesthetic appeal.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有一种简单的审美吸引力。
words.en: Concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty.

words.ex: He changed his job because of his background.
words.ex_cn: 他因为自己的背景换了工作。
words.en: The background is the situation that exists at a particular time, or the situation in which something happens, which helps to explain it.

words.ex: The smell of bread permeate the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫了整个厨房。
words.en: If something permeates a place, it spreads throughout it.

words.ex: Her story inspires me to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 她的故事激励我更加努力。
words.en: If someone or something inspires you to do something new or unusual, they make you want to do it.

words.tr:
n. 外星人；外国人；外侨；
adj. 外国的；陌生的；相异的；
words.ex: The boy saw an alien in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在森林里看到了一个外星人。
words.en: An alien is someone who is not a citizen of the country in which they live, or a creature from outer space.

words.ex: The main criterion for winning is fairness.
words.ex_cn: 获胜的主要标准是公平。
words.en: A criterion is a principle or standard by which something may be judged or decided.

words.ex: The historian wrote a book about ancient Rome.
words.ex_cn: 这位历史学家写了一本关于古罗马的书。
words.en: A historian is a person who studies or writes about history; an expert in history.

words.tr:
adj. 抽象的；非具体的；
n. 摘要；概要；抽象派艺术作品；
words.ex: The painting shows an abstract shape.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画展示了一个抽象的形状。
words.en: An abstract idea or way of thinking is based on general ideas rather than on real things and events.

words.ex: The story had a graphic description of the battle.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事对战斗的描述非常生动。
words.en: A graphic is a visual representation of data or information, such as a chart, diagram, or picture.

words.ex: He paints on a canvas with oil colors.
words.ex_cn: 他用油画颜料在帆布上作画。
words.en: A strong, coarse unbleached cloth made from hemp, flax, cotton, or a similar yarn, used to make items such as sails and tents and as a surface for oil painting.

words.ex: The painter portrays a happy family in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 这位画家在画中描绘了一个幸福的家庭。
words.en: To portray someone or something means to show or represent them in a painting, film, book, or other artistic work.

words.tr: v. 复制；复印；再做一次；
words.ex: He duplicated the file to save a copy.
words.ex_cn: 他复制了该文件以保存一份副本。
words.en: To duplicate something means to make an exact copy of it.

words.tr: n. 陶器；制陶手艺；陶器作坊；
words.ex: He makes pottery in his backyard studio.
words.ex_cn: 他在后院的工作室制作陶器。
words.en: Objects such as pots, dishes, and vases that are made out of clay and then baked at high temperatures to make them hard.

words.tr:
n. 陶瓷制品；陶瓷器；
adj. 陶质的；制陶的；
words.ex: He bought a ceramic bowl at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一个陶瓷碗。
words.en: Ceramic is a hard material that is made by baking clay or similar substances at high temperatures. It is used to make things such as tiles, dishes, and statues.

words.ex: The statue is made of bronze.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像由青铜制成。
words.en: Bronze is a yellowish-brown metal which is a mixture of copper and tin.

words.tr: n. 雕刻（术）；雕塑品；雕刻品；
words.ex: He made a beautiful sculpture from clay.
words.ex_cn: 他用黏土做了一件精美的雕刻。
words.en: Sculpture is the art of making two- or three-dimensional representative or abstract forms, especially by carving stone or wood or by casting metal or plaster.

words.ex: He carved the meat with a sharp knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用一把锋利的刀切开了肉。
words.en: To carve means to cut into a hard material in order to produce an object, design, or inscription.

words.tr:
n. 半身像；胸部；搜捕
v. 打碎；搜捕
adj. 破产的；打碎的
words.ex: The museum has a marble bust of the ancient king.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆里有一座古代国王的大理石半身像。
words.en: A bust is a sculpture of a person's head, shoulders, and chest. As a verb, to bust means to break something, to arrest someone, or to go bankrupt.

words.ex: He wears a badge on his shirt.
words.ex_cn: 他衬衫上戴着一枚徽章。
words.en: A badge is a small piece of metal, plastic, or cloth which you wear in order to show people that you have a particular rank, job, or belong to a particular group.

chapters.name: 人文社会：智慧结晶 - 品味文学

words.ex: He loves reading literary books.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读文学书籍。
words.en: Literary means concerned with or connected with the writing, study, or appreciation of literature.

words.ex: He loves reading English literature.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢阅读英语文学。
words.en: Literature consists of written works, especially those considered to have artistic or intellectual value.

words.ex: He took his words in a literal sense.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的话按字面意思理解。
words.en: If you describe something as the literal truth or a literal fact, you are emphasizing that it is true.

words.ex: The renaissance brought new art and ideas to Europe.
words.ex_cn: 文艺复兴为欧洲带来了新的艺术和思想。
words.en: The Renaissance was a period in European history marking the transition from the Middle Ages to modernity and covering the 15th and 16th centuries, characterized by an effort to revive and surpass ideas and achievements of classical antiquity.

words.ex: The baby was sleeping in the cradle.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿正在吊架里睡觉。
words.en: A cradle is a small bed for a baby, which can be rocked from side to side. It can also refer to the place or period in which something begins or is developed.

words.ex: The castle is a medieval building.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是一座中世纪的建筑。
words.en: Relating to the Middle Ages, the period in European history from about the 5th century to the 15th century.

words.ex: He is the author of this book.
words.ex_cn: 他是这本书的作者。
words.en: An author is a person who writes books, stories, or articles, especially as a job.

words.ex: The audience clapped loudly after the show.
words.ex_cn: 演出结束后，观众热烈鼓掌。
words.en: The group of spectators at a public event; listeners or viewers collectively, especially those attending a performance or reading a particular work.

words.ex: He could not conceive a world without technology.
words.ex_cn: 他无法设想一个没有科技的世界。
words.en: To conceive means to form or devise a plan or idea in the mind; to become pregnant.

words.ex: He contrived to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他设法按时完成了项目。
words.en: If you contrive an event or situation, you succeed in making it happen, often by tricking someone.

words.ex: The painting is a beautiful creation of the artist.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是艺术家的一个美丽作品。
words.en: The act or process of bringing something into existence.

words.tr:
adj. 原来的；有创造性的；原版的；新颖的；
n. 原件；原稿；
words.ex: This is the original book I bought last year.
words.ex_cn: 这是我去年买的那本原版书。
words.en: An original piece of writing or music was written recently and has not been published or performed before.

words.tr: v. 授权；命名；给...权利（或资格）
words.ex: This book entitles you to a free gift.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使你有资格获得一份免费礼物。
words.en: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

words.ex: He compiles data from many surveys.
words.ex_cn: 他汇编来自许多调查的数据。
words.en: To compile means to collect information from different places and arrange it in a book, report, or list.

words.ex: The painting depicts a quiet village at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一个宁静的村庄在日落时分的景象。
words.en: To depict someone or something means to show or represent them in a work of art such as a drawing or painting.

words.ex: He unfolded the map on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他把地图在桌子上展开。
words.en: To open or spread out something that is folded; to develop or be revealed.

words.ex: The letter revealed his secret.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他的秘密。
words.en: To reveal something means to make known something that was previously secret or unknown.

words.tr: v. 代表；表现；体现；相当于；
words.ex: He represents his country in the competition.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中代表他的国家。
words.en: If someone represents a person or group of people, they act on behalf of that person or group.

words.ex: The soil degrades over time without proper care.
words.ex_cn: 如果没有适当照料，土壤会逐渐退化。
words.en: If something degrades or is degraded, it becomes worse in quality, or weaker in power or status.

words.ex: He will modify the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会更改计划。
words.en: To change something slightly, especially in order to make it more suitable for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The comparison of the two phones helped me decide.
words.ex_cn: 对这两部手机的比较帮助我做出了决定。
words.en: When you make a comparison, you consider two or more things and discover the differences or similarities between them.

words.ex: They wrote a love letter every day, and it became their romance.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天写一封情书，这成为了他们的浪漫史。
words.en: Romance refers to the feelings and behaviors characteristic of love, especially in its early stages, or a story, movie, or other work dealing with love in a sentimental or idealized way.

words.ex: The painting is considered a masterpiece by art critics.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画被艺术评论家视为杰作。
words.en: A masterpiece is a work of art such as a painting, film, or book that is made with great skill and is considered to be the best work of a particular artist or writer.

words.ex: He found an old manuscript in the library.
words.ex_cn: 他在图书馆里发现了一份旧手稿。
words.en: A manuscript is a handwritten or typed document, especially a writer's first version of a book before it is published.

words.ex: He loves reading science fiction.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读科幻小说。
words.en: Fiction refers to literature in the form of prose, especially novels, that describes imaginary events and people.

words.ex: It's a myth that eating late at night causes weight gain.
words.ex_cn: 晚上吃东西会导致发胖，这是一种错误观念。
words.en: A myth is a traditional story, especially one concerning the early history of a people or explaining some natural or social phenomenon, and typically involving supernatural beings or events.

words.tr: n. 神话；神话学；神话集；
words.ex: He loves reading Greek mythology.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读希腊神话。
words.en: Mythology is a collection of myths, especially one belonging to a particular religious or cultural tradition.

words.ex: The legend says a dragon lives in the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 传说有一条龙住在山里。
words.en: A legend is a very old and popular story that may be true or may be imaginary.

words.ex: The movie is a satire about politicians.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部关于政治家的讽刺作品。
words.en: A way of criticizing people or ideas in a humorous way, especially in order to make a political point, or a piece of writing that uses this style.

words.ex: The dragon is an imaginary creature.
words.ex_cn: 龙是一种想象中的生物。
words.en: An imaginary person, place, or thing is one that does not exist or is not real, but that people think about or talk about.

words.ex: The engineer built a prototype of the new car.
words.ex_cn: 工程师制作了这辆新车的原型。
words.en: A prototype is the first or original example of something that has been or will be copied or developed; it is a model or preliminary version.

words.ex: The skeleton of the dinosaur is displayed in the museum.
words.ex_cn: 恐龙的骨架在博物馆里展出。
words.en: The internal structure that supports and gives shape to a person, animal, or plant, composed of bones and cartilage in vertebrates.

words.ex: He read a biography of Nelson Mandela.
words.ex_cn: 他读了一本关于纳尔逊·曼德拉的传记。
words.en: A biography is a detailed description of a person's life. It involves more than just the basic facts like education, work, relationships, and death; it portrays a person's experience of these life events.

words.ex: He loves reading poetry before bed.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在睡前读诗歌。
words.en: Poetry is the expression of ideas and feelings through the use of distinctive style and rhythm.

words.ex: He writes a verse every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上写一首诗。
words.en: A verse is one of the parts into which a poem, a song, or a chapter of the Bible or the Koran is divided.

words.ex: He writes simple prose every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天写简单的散文。
words.en: Prose is written language in its ordinary form, without metrical structure.

words.tr:
n. 叙述；叙事；
adj. 叙述性的；
words.ex: He told a simple narrative about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个关于他童年的简单故事。
words.en: A narrative is a story or an account of a series of events.

words.ex: The volume of the box is 10 cubic meters.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子的体积是10立方米。
words.en: A volume is a book, especially one that is part of a series of books. It can also refer to the amount of space that a substance or object occupies, or the level of sound produced by a television, radio, etc.

words.ex: He used an idiom to explain his idea.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个成语来解释他的想法。
words.en: An idiom is a group of words in a fixed order that have a particular meaning that is different from the meanings of each word on its own.

words.tr:
n. 轮廓；纲要；
v. 描画轮廓；概述；
words.ex: The artist drew the outline of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家画出了山的轮廓。
words.en: An outline is a line that shows or forms the outer edge of something, or a general description or plan showing the essential features of something but not the detail.

words.tr:
n. 摘录；摘要
v. 摘录；引用
words.ex: He read an excerpt from the book.
words.ex_cn: 他读了这本书的一段摘录。
words.en: An excerpt is a short piece of writing or music which is taken from a larger piece.

words.ex: He wrote a short paragraph about his vacation.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一段关于他假期的短文。
words.en: A paragraph is a section of a piece of writing, usually consisting of several sentences dealing with a single subject. The first sentence of a paragraph typically starts on a new line.

words.tr: n. 差额；边缘；净利润；余地；
words.ex: The profit margin is five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 利润差额是五美元。
words.en: The margin is the edge or border of something, or the difference between two amounts, especially the difference between the cost of producing something and the price it is sold for.

words.ex: He skipped the hard question and moved to the next one.
words.ex_cn: 他略过了难题，继续做下一题。
words.en: To move lightly and quickly, making a small jump after each step.

words.ex: The stray dog wandered into the backyard.
words.ex_cn: 这只走失的狗走进了后院。
words.en: If someone or something strays, they wander away from where they are supposed to be.

chapters.name: 人文社会：智慧结晶 - 华美建筑

words.ex: The architect showed us the blueprint of the new house.
words.ex_cn: 建筑师给我们看了新房子的蓝图。
words.en: A blueprint is a detailed plan or design of something, often used in the context of buildings or machinery, which shows how it is to be made or how it will work.

words.ex: He lives in a big mansion near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边的一座大宅子里。
words.en: A mansion is a very large, impressive house, especially one that is the home of a wealthy or important person.

words.ex: The soldiers defended the fort during the battle.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在战斗中保卫了堡垒。
words.en: A fort is a strong building or a place with a wall or fence around it where soldiers can stay and be safe from the enemy.

words.ex: One aspect of learning English is practicing speaking.
words.ex_cn: 学习英语的一个方面是练习口语。
words.en: An aspect of something is one of the parts of its character or nature.

words.ex: This is a good example of teamwork.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个团队合作的好例子。
words.en: An example is a particular instance of something that is representative of a group or used to illustrate a point.

words.ex: They laid new tile in the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 他们在厨房铺了新的瓷砖。
words.en: A tile is a flat piece of baked clay, carpet, cork, or other material, used especially for covering roofs and floors.

words.ex: The church has a big dome above the altar.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的祭坛上方有一个大穹顶。
words.en: A dome is a rounded vault made of either curved segments or a shell of revolution, meaning an arch rotated around its central vertical axis.

words.ex: The bridge has a stone arch.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥有一个石拱。
words.en: An arch is a structure that is curved at the top and is usually made of stone or brick. Arches are often used to support the weight of a bridge or the roof of a building.

words.ex: He crossed the threshold of adulthood at 18.
words.ex_cn: 他在18岁时进入了成年的起始点。
words.en: The threshold of something is the point at which it begins or changes.

words.ex: He sits on the porch and drinks coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在门廊上喝咖啡。
words.en: A porch is a covered shelter projecting in front of the entrance of a building.

words.ex: He walked up the staircase to his room.
words.ex_cn: 他走上楼梯去了他的房间。
words.en: A staircase is a set of stairs inside a building, often including the supporting structure, the handrails, and sometimes the landings at the top and bottom.

words.tr:
n. 清漆；漆面；光泽面
v. 给…涂上清漆
words.ex: He put varnish on the wooden table.
words.ex_cn: 他在木桌上涂了清漆。
words.en: Varnish is a transparent, hard, protective finish or film primarily used in wood finishing but also for other materials. Varnish is traditionally a combination of a drying oil, a resin, and a thinner or solvent.

words.ex: The toys are in the basement.
words.ex_cn: 玩具在地下室里。
words.en: The basement of a building is a room or area that is partly or completely below ground level.

words.ex: He keeps apples in the cellar.
words.ex_cn: 他把苹果存放在地窖里。
words.en: A cellar is a room underneath a house, often used for storing things such as wine or coal.

words.tr:
v. 使脱落；去除；
n. 棚屋；
words.ex: The tree sheds its leaves in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在秋天落叶。
words.en: A shed is a small building, usually made of wood, used for storing things such as garden tools. When something sheds, it loses its covering, such as leaves or hair, or it gets rid of something it no longer needs.

words.tr:
n. 划分；隔离物；分割
v. 分开；隔开
words.ex: The partition of the room made it more private.
words.ex_cn: 房间的隔断让它更私密了。
words.en: A partition is a wall, screen, or divider that separates one part of a room, vehicle, or other space from another.

words.ex: The rainwater drains into the street.
words.ex_cn: 雨水排入街道。
words.en: If you drain something, you remove the liquid from it, usually by pouring it away or by allowing it to flow away. If something drains, the liquid flows away from it.

words.ex: The city improved its drainage system after the flood.
words.ex_cn: 洪水之后，这座城市改进了它的排水系统。
words.en: Drainage is the system or process by which water or other liquids are drained from a place.

words.ex: Open the window to ventilate the room.
words.ex_cn: 打开窗户给房间通风。
words.en: To ventilate means to cause fresh air to enter and move around a room, building, etc., or to express your opinions or feelings about something openly.

words.ex: The smoke came out of the vent.
words.ex_cn: 烟从排气口飘了出来。
words.en: A vent is a hole or opening that allows air, gas, or liquid to pass out of or into a confined space.

words.tr:
v. 建造；构造；
n. 概念；
words.ex: They construct houses with bricks.
words.ex_cn: 他们用砖块建造房屋。
words.en: To construct something means to build or create it, usually something large such as a building, road, or machine.

words.tr:
n. 楔子；三角木；楔形物
v. 把…楔住 ；将…挤入（或塞进、插入）
words.ex: He used a wedge to split the wood.
words.ex_cn: 他用楔子把木头劈开。
words.en: A wedge is a piece of wood, metal, or other material with one thick end and one thin edge, used to keep something in position or to split something apart.

words.ex: They erect a flagpole in the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们在公园里竖立一根旗杆。
words.en: If people erect something such as a building, bridge, or barrier, they build it or create it.

words.ex: We decorate the room for the party.
words.ex_cn: 我们为派对装饰房间。
words.en: To make something look more attractive by putting things on it or around it.

words.ex: The tree has many colorful ornaments.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树上有许多彩色的装饰品。
words.en: An ornament is an object that is used to make something look more attractive but is usually considered to have no practical purpose.

chapters.name: 人文社会：智慧结晶 - 宗教风俗

words.tr: adj. 普遍的；流行的；盛行的；
words.ex: Smoking is prevalent in that country.
words.ex_cn: 在那个国家，吸烟很普遍。
words.en: If a condition, practice, or belief is prevalent, it is common or widespread.

words.ex: He practices his religion every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都实践自己的宗教信仰。
words.en: Religion is the belief in and worship of a superhuman controlling power, especially a personal God or gods.

words.ex: He visits a religious temple every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都去一座宗教寺庙。
words.en: Relating to or believing in a religion.

words.ex: He converts old paper into new notebooks.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧纸张转换成新笔记本。
words.en: To change something into a different form or to change someone's beliefs, especially their religious beliefs.

words.ex: The conversion of water into steam takes heat.
words.ex_cn: 水变成蒸汽需要热量。
words.en: The process of changing or causing something to change from one form to another.

words.tr: n. （宗教等的）仪式；例行习惯；
words.ex: The village holds a ritual every spring to pray for good weather.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄每年春天都举行一个仪式，祈求好天气。
words.en: A ritual is a religious service or other ceremony which involves a series of actions performed in a fixed order.

words.ex: The temple is a divine place.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙是神的圣地。
words.en: Something that is divine relates to a god or goddess.

words.tr:
n. 天主教徒；
adj. 天主教的；
words.ex: He is a catholic who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名每周日都去教堂的天主教徒。
words.en: If you describe a collection of things or people as catholic, you are emphasizing that it is varied and includes many different types of things or people.

words.ex: The pope speaks to millions of people every year.
words.ex_cn: 教皇每年向数百万人讲话。
words.en: The Pope is the bishop of Rome and the leader of the worldwide Catholic Church.

words.tr:
adj. 首要的；大红色的
n. 红衣主教；枢机主教；基数
words.ex: This is a cardinal rule in our school.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们学校的一项首要规则。
words.en: A cardinal rule or quality is the most important one.

words.ex: The priest said a prayer for the sick.
words.ex_cn: 牧师为病人祈祷。
words.en: A priest is a person who is qualified to perform religious duties and ceremonies in a Christian church.

words.ex: The missionary taught children in a small village.
words.ex_cn: 这位传教士在一个小村庄里教孩子们。
words.en: A missionary is a person who is sent to a foreign country to spread a religion.

words.ex: He preaches kindness every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都宣扬仁爱。
words.en: If you preach, you give a talk on a religious or moral subject during a religious service.

words.ex: The priest gave a long sermon about kindness.
words.ex_cn: 牧师做了一场关于仁爱的长时间布道。
words.en: A sermon is a talk on a religious or moral subject, especially one given during a church service.

words.ex: The church teaches its doctrine to all members.
words.ex_cn: 教会向所有成员传授它的教义。
words.en: A doctrine is a set of beliefs or principles that are taught or accepted by a particular group, especially in religion or politics.

words.ex: The prophet told the people about the coming storm.
words.ex_cn: 预言者告诉人们即将到来的风暴。
words.en: A prophet is a person who is believed to be chosen by God to lead the people and to tell them what God wants them to do.

words.ex: The old woman made a prophecy about the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那位老妇人预言了会有雨。
words.en: A prophecy is a statement that something will happen in the future, especially one made by someone with religious or magical powers.

words.tr: adj. 预言的；预示的；先知的
words.ex: His words were prophetic when the storm came.
words.ex_cn: 当风暴来临时，他的话应验了。
words.en: If something was prophetic, it described or suggested something that did actually happen later.

words.ex: He believed his destiny was to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他相信自己的命运是成为一名医生。
words.en: Destiny is the force which some people believe controls the things that happen to you in your life.

words.ex: The pilgrim walked to the holy place.
words.ex_cn: 朝圣者步行前往圣地。
words.en: A pilgrim is a person who journeys to a sacred place for religious reasons.

words.ex: He took an oath to tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓要说出真相。
words.en: An oath is a formal promise, especially one made in a court of law or a religious ceremony, or a swear word.

words.tr:
adj. 恶毒的；
n. 邪恶；罪恶；
words.ex: The evil king punished innocent people.
words.ex_cn: 这个恶毒的国王惩罚了无辜的人。
words.en: Evil is a powerful force that some people believe to exist, and which causes wicked and bad things to happen.

words.ex: They found paradise on a small island.
words.ex_cn: 他们在一个小岛上找到了天堂。
words.en: Paradise is a place of ideal beauty or loveliness, or a state of supreme happiness.

words.ex: She blesses her children every morning.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上为孩子们祝福。
words.en: If someone is blessed with a particular good quality or skill, they have that good quality or skill.

words.ex: She felt pure bliss when she held her newborn baby.
words.ex_cn: 当她抱住新生儿时，感受到了无上的幸福。
words.en: Bliss is a state of complete happiness.

words.ex: The cathedral has tall towers and stained glass windows.
words.ex_cn: 这座大教堂有高高的塔楼和彩绘玻璃窗。
words.en: A cathedral is a very large and important church which has a bishop in charge of it.

words.ex: He walks to the chapel every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每个星期天都去小教堂。
words.en: A chapel is a small building or room used for Christian worship, typically one that is not a parish church.

words.ex: It is customary to shake hands when you meet someone.
words.ex_cn: 见面时握手是习惯做法。
words.en: Something that is customary is normal because it is the way something is usually done.

words.ex: He wears conventional clothes to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿传统服装去上班。
words.en: Conventional ideas, methods, or systems are the ones that are generally accepted and used, and that have been used for a long time.

words.ex: He uses an unorthodox method to teach math.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种非传统的方法教数学。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour, beliefs, or customs as unorthodox, you mean that they are different from what is generally accepted.

words.tr: n. 迷信；迷信观念（或思想）；
words.ex: He avoids walking under ladders because of superstition.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迷信而不愿从梯子下走过。
words.en: A superstition is a belief or practice resulting from ignorance, fear of the unknown, trust in magic or chance, or a false conception of causation.

chapters.name: 人文社会：笑看沉浮

words.ex: The new regime changed the tax laws.
words.ex_cn: 新的管理制度改变了税法。
words.en: A regime is the set of rules or the way that a country or organization is governed, especially when it is considered to be strict or unfair.

words.ex: The old house has a colonial style.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子具有殖民地风格。
words.en: Colonial means relating to a system or period of colonization, or to the people who live in a colony.

words.ex: The country gained independence in 1960.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在1960年获得了独立。
words.en: Independence is the freedom from control or influence of others, allowing one to make decisions and act on one's own.

words.ex: He believes in capitalism and owns a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他相信资本主义，并拥有一家小企业。
words.en: Capitalism is an economic system in which the means of production are privately owned and operated for profit in a competitive market.

words.ex: The country still has a monarchy with a king as the head of state.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家仍然实行君主制，国王是国家元首。
words.en: A monarchy is a form of government in which a country is ruled by a monarch, such as a king or queen.

words.ex: The queen's reign lasted 70 years.
words.ex_cn: 女王的统治持续了70年。
words.en: The period during which a sovereign rules; to hold royal office; to prevail

words.ex: The imperial palace was built long ago.
words.ex_cn: 这座帝国宫殿是很久以前建造的。
words.en: relating to an empire or an emperor; majestic or superior in quality or size

words.tr: n. 最高权威；王权；威严
words.ex: The king showed his majesty to the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 国王向人群展示了他的威严。
words.en: If you talk about the majesty of something, you are emphasizing its great beauty, scale, or power.

words.tr:
n. 最高统治者；君主；元首
adj. 独立自主的；拥有最高统治权的
words.ex: The sovereign makes important decisions for the country.
words.ex_cn: 君主为国家做出重要决定。
words.en: A sovereign is a king, queen, or other supreme ruler.

words.ex: The king sat on the throne.
words.ex_cn: 国王坐在王位上。
words.en: The throne is the special chair used by a king, queen, or emperor during ceremonies, or the position of being a ruler.

words.ex: The university has great prestige for its research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学因其研究而享有很高的声望。
words.en: The widespread respect and admiration felt for someone or something on the basis of a perception of their achievements or quality.

words.tr: n. 联邦；共和国；联合体；
words.ex: Australia is a member of the Commonwealth.
words.ex_cn: 澳大利亚是联邦的成员。
words.en: A commonwealth is a traditional English term for a political community founded for the common good. Historically, it has been synonymous with 'republic'.

words.tr: adj. 联邦的；联邦制的；联邦政府的；
words.ex: The federal government passed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 联邦政府通过了一项新法律。
words.en: A federal system of government is one in which there is a central government and separate governments for each of the states or regions.

words.ex: The countries formed a federation to share resources.
words.ex_cn: 这些国家组成了一个联盟来共享资源。
words.en: A federation is a group of states or organizations that have joined together to form a single entity with a central government or authority.

words.ex: The two parties formed a coalition to win the election.
words.ex_cn: 这两个政党联合起来以赢得选举。
words.en: A coalition is a temporary alliance for combined action, especially of political parties forming a government.

words.ex: The two countries formed an alliance to fight the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家结成联盟以对抗敌人。
words.en: An alliance is a group of countries or political parties that are formally united and working together because they have similar aims.

words.tr:
adj. 当前的；流通的；
n. （水、气、电）流；趋势；
words.ex: The current weather is very hot.
words.ex_cn: 当前的天气非常热。
words.en: belonging to the present time; happening or being used or done now

words.ex: He kept the dishes in the cabinet.
words.ex_cn: 他把盘子放在储藏柜里。
words.en: A cabinet is a piece of furniture with doors and shelves or drawers, used for storing or showing things. In politics, a cabinet is a group of people who are chosen by a head of state to give advice and to help set government policy.

words.ex: The dominant color in the room is blue.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间占优势的颜色是蓝色。
words.en: Someone or something that is dominant is more powerful, successful, influential, or noticeable than other people or things.

words.ex: The committee will convene tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 委员会明天将召开会议。
words.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. They can also be said to convene when they meet.

words.ex: The climbers reached the summit of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 登山者到达了山顶。
words.en: The highest point of a hill or mountain; a meeting between heads of government.

words.tr: n. 代表大会；议会；国会；
words.ex: The congress met to discuss new laws.
words.ex_cn: 代表大会召开以讨论新法律。
words.en: A congress is a formal meeting of representatives, as of various nations, to discuss problems or to make decisions.

words.ex: The global climate conference was held in Paris.
words.ex_cn: 全球气候大会在巴黎举行。
words.en: A conference is a meeting of people who share the same interests or profession.

words.ex: It is a convention to shake hands when you meet someone.
words.ex_cn: 见面时握手是一种习俗。
words.en: A convention is a large meeting of an organization or political group, or a way of behaving that is considered to be correct or polite by most people in a society.

words.ex: He will assemble the toy for his son.
words.ex_cn: 他将为儿子组装玩具。
words.en: If people assemble or if someone assembles them, they come together in a group, usually for a particular purpose such as a meeting.

words.ex: We will review the meeting agenda tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天将审查会议议程。
words.en: An agenda is a list or plan of things to be done or considered, especially in a meeting.

words.ex: The committee meets every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 委员会每周一开会。
words.en: A committee is a group of people who are chosen to do a particular job or make decisions on behalf of a larger group.

words.tr: n. 理事会；委员会；议会；
words.ex: The city council made a new rule about recycling.
words.ex_cn: 市政府理事会制定了关于回收的新规定。
words.en: A council is a group of people who are elected to govern a local area such as a city or, in Britain, a county.

words.ex: The statesman spoke wisely to calm the nation.
words.ex_cn: 这位政治家明智地讲话以安抚国家。
words.en: A statesman is a respected political leader or figure, especially one who has had a long and successful career in politics.

words.tr: n. 外交官；会耍手腕儿的人
words.ex: The diplomat met the president yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 这位外交官昨天会见了总统。
words.en: A diplomat is a person who represents their country in a foreign country, managing political relations and negotiations.

words.ex: He is the premier player on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他是队里最优秀的球员。
words.en: The premier is the leader of the government in some countries, equivalent to a prime minister.

words.ex: The senator speaks to the people every week.
words.ex_cn: 这位参议员每周都对人民讲话。
words.en: A senator is a member of a senate, which is a governing body in many countries, especially in the United States.

words.tr: n. 对应物；相当之物；副本；
words.ex: The CEO's counterpart in China signed the agreement.
words.ex_cn: 中国方面的对应人物签署了协议。
words.en: Someone's or something's counterpart is another person or thing that has a similar function or position in a different place.

words.ex: He is a candidate for the mayor position.
words.ex_cn: 他是市长职位的候选人。
words.en: A candidate is someone who is being considered for a position, for example someone who is running in an election or applying for a job.

words.ex: The two colors distinguish the two teams.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色使两个队伍有所不同。
words.en: If you can distinguish one thing from another, you can see or understand how they are different.

words.ex: His pursuit of happiness made him work hard every day.
